sample_tweets.text: ⚠️ UNPATCHED CRITICAL LMCACHE FLAW LETS UNAUTHENTICATED ATTACKERS RUN CODE ON LLM CACHE SERVERS (CVE-2026-105192, CVSS 9.8)  JFrog Security Research has disclosed an unauthenticated remote code execution flaw in LMCache, a KV-cache layer for LLM inference used with engines such as vLLM. No fixed release is available yet.  • Where: multiprocess (distributed) mode opens a ZeroMQ socket, port 5555 by default, with no authentication • How: one message type is decoded with Python pickle before the request handler runs, so a single crafted message runs code as the LMCache process user, which is root in the official container images • Affected: v0.3.9 through v0.5.5 (the latest PyPI release), plus the v0.5.6 release candidates through rc3 and the dev branch • Exposure: the socket binds to localhost by default. The 9.8 score applies when an operator binds it to a routable address, the documented multi-node setup. LMCache running only inside a vLLM process does not open this port  ⚠️ Analyst Note: No exploitation in the wild has been reported, and the flaw is not in CISA KEV. Until a patch ships, JFrog advises keeping the multiprocess port on localhost or a trusted cluster network. A firewall narrows who can reach it, but any host that can still connect can run code.  Source: research.jfrog.com/vulnerabi… #DDW #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity #LMCache #vLLM #CVE #AISecurity

🇦🇷 🚨 GOVERNMENT OF TUCUMÁN (ARGENTINA) DATABASE ALLEGEDLY LEAKED, 90,000 RECORDS CLAIMED  A hacktivist-style group on an underground forum claims to have leaked a database belonging to the Government of Tucumán, Argentina, in a post titled "90K registros".  The listing shows: * Claimed victim: Gobierno de Tucumán (provincial government) * Claimed volume: 90,000 records * Data per the listing: names, ID numbers, dates of birth, localities, street addresses and phone numbers * Sample rows of residents (redacted here)  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If genuine, a 90,000-row citizen file with ID numbers, birth dates, addresses and phones is enough for impersonation, SIM-swap attempts and targeted scams against Tucumán residents. The group posts many Latin American government databases in quick succession, and the source system inside the provincial government is not named, so this could be a single portal or program database rather than a core registry. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that Tucumán government systems were breached.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Argentina #Tucuman #Government #DataLeak #PII #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🚨 POELLM BOTNET INFECTS 3,400+ EXPOSED AI AND DEV SERVERS, HIDES ITS C2 ADDRESS IN A POEM ON GITHUB  Lumen's Black Lotus Labs says the PoeLLM malware has hit more than 3,400 servers since April 2026, mostly vulnerable internet-facing LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea deployments, with possible targeting of Ivanti Sentry. Most victims are in the US and Western Europe.  • The malware works out its C2 IP address from four keywords in a poem kept in a GitHub repository. The actor has edited the poem 11 times since April 13, each time pointing the bots to a new server • Infected hosts mine cryptocurrency with XMRig and Iron and are reused to scan for and exploit new victims • Several C2 servers ran on hijacked routers with vulnerable admin pages • Lumen says a LiteLLM endpoint tied to command-injection flaw CVE-2026-42271 was likely the exploitation path • Lumen links PoeLLM to an Italian-speaking actor, says the campaign appears financially motivated, and has blocked traffic to and from its C2 servers  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Activity peaked at roughly 800 active bots a day. Self-hosted AI services combine known bugs with powerful hardware, which makes them attractive mining targets. Keep LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea patched and off the open internet, and check network logs against the IOCs Lumen published.  Source: lumen.com/blog/en-us/canto-i… #DDW #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity #Botnet #Malware #AISecurity #Cryptomining

🇫🇷 🚨 FRANCE TRAVAIL EMPLOYEE DATABASE ALLEGEDLY FOR SALE, 62,848 ROWS CLAIMED  A threat actor on an underground forum is selling what they claim is a France Travail database that "only contains employee data", 62,848 rows, in a listing titled "France Travail September 2026".  The listing shows: * Claimed source: France Travail, the French public employment service (formerly Pôle emploi) * Data scope: agency staff, not jobseekers * Fields: names, job function and sub-role, landline and mobile numbers, emails, site and department, region, structure type, internal system identifiers, access-authorization profile and photo URL * Sample rows of staff records (redacted here)  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If genuine, this is a staff directory of a large public agency: names, roles, direct phone lines and internal IDs are exactly what attackers need for convincing phishing and help-desk social engineering against France Travail employees, which can open the door to jobseeker data. France Travail has reported several data incidents since 2024, so recycled or merged data is possible and the "September 2026" label is the seller's own. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation of a new France Travail breach.  #DDW #DarkWeb #France #FranceTravail #Government #DataLeak #GDPR #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🚨 ATTACKERS HIJACKED THREE COUNTRY-CODE DOMAIN REGISTRIES AND OBTAINED HTTPS CERTIFICATES FOR GOOGLE DOMAINS  Google says attackers compromised the third-party operators of the .gh (Ghana), .sl (Sierra Leone) and .as (American Samoa) top-level domains, changed authoritative DNS records, and got unauthorized HTTPS certificates for several Google domains and for domains of other organizations.  • Google says its own systems were not compromised, and it has no reason to believe the issuing Certificate Authorities did anything wrong • Chrome blocked the rogue certificates through CRLSets, and the CAs revoked them for other browsers and clients • Certificate Transparency logs showed more victims, including several large global brands and popular online services, which Chrome also blocked • Google learned of the hijacks last week and did not say who was behind them or how the registries were breached • Chrome users do not need to do anything  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Google warns its analysis may not have found every affected domain, and Chrome's blocking does not protect users of other browsers. Google says any domain ending in .gh, .sl or .as was put at risk. Domain owners should monitor Certificate Transparency logs for their names and lock down which CAs may issue for them.  Official: blog.google/security/chromes… #DDW #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity #DNS #DNSHijacking #Google #Chrome

🇧🇷 🚨 CRUZEIRO DO SUL EDUCACIONAL AND 12 BRAZILIAN UNIVERSITIES ALLEGEDLY BREACHED, 630M+ RECORDS CLAIMED  A threat actor on an underground forum claims to have fully compromised Cruzeiro do Sul Educacional, one of Brazil's largest private education groups, plus 12 subsidiaries including Unicid, Universidade Positivo, Unipe, Braz Cubas, Unifran, UDF, CEUNSP, Cesuca, FSG, Módulo, FASS and FAPIP.  The listing claims: * 630M+ rows dumped across the group's environment * 450,000+ identity-provider records (profiles, logins, account status) * 107,000+ signed contracts and PDFs with CPF numbers and PII * 25,884 identity records with tax IDs, emails, roles and passwords * 3,127 Microsoft 365 staff accounts and 340 privileged accounts * 27 internal databases plus payroll, salary, HR benefit and dependent data * A file tree listing 38,198 credentials for employees and students  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: If genuine, this would expose students and staff across 13 institutions at once. Plaintext and hashed passwords plus M365 and privileged accounts raise the risk of account takeover and follow-on phishing, while CPF, payroll and bank data are prime material for identity fraud. "630 million rows" counts database rows, not unique people. The actor account is brand new. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that Cruzeiro do Sul systems were breached; under Brazil's LGPD a confirmed incident would trigger ANPD and data-subject notification.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Brazil #CruzeiroDoSul #Education #DataBreach #LGPD #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🚨 CISCO PATCHES CVSS 9.8 UNAUTHENTICATED ROOT RCE FLAWS IN NX-OS FOR NEXUS 3000 AND 9000 SWITCHES  Cisco published its October 7, 2026 bundled advisories, including three NX-OS advisories covering five CVSS 9.8 flaws that let a remote, unauthenticated attacker run code as root or crash the switch.  • CVE-2026-76465: MPLS OAM, triggered by a crafted MPLS echo-request (Nexus 3000 / 9000 standalone) • CVE-2026-76485, CVE-2026-76486, CVE-2026-76501: Next Generation OAM (NGOAM), crafted packets to an IP interface • CVE-2026-76471: NX-API, crafted HTTP request (also UCS 6300 Fabric Interconnects, where credentials are needed and Cisco rates it High) • Impact: arbitrary code with root privileges, or process crashes and device reload (DoS) • Workarounds: none. Fixed NX-OS software is available; Cisco also released temporary Live Protect shields, and disabling unused MPLS OAM or NGOAM removes the attack vector • Exposure: MPLS OAM and NX-API are disabled by default; the NGOAM flaws need NGOAM enabled (two also need SRv6 or NV Overlay)  ⚠️ Analyst Note: Cisco PSIRT says it is not aware of public announcements or malicious use, and the flaws were found in internal testing. None are in CISA KEV at handoff. Data-center switches are high-value targets, so check whether these features are enabled and patch quickly.  Official: sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/secu… #DDW #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity #Cisco #NXOS #CVE #PatchNow

🇨🇴 🚨 NUEVA EPS UPDATE: 34,410 AMAZONAS HEALTH RECORDS ALLEGEDLY LEAKED, 48-HOUR ULTIMATUM ISSUED  A threat actor on an underground forum claims a third partial leak of data allegedly taken from Nueva EPS, Colombia's largest health insurer, this time 34,410 records from the Amazonas department.  The listing shows: * Title: "Amazonas - 34k Sensitive healthcare records" * Claimed release: "34,410 records from Amazonas" * A 48-hour ultimatum telling Nueva EPS to make contact * A threat that the next leak "will expose over 1 million records from Santander" * A message to Colombians saying institutions "have failed" them * A field list covering ID numbers, names, DOB, sex, ethnicity and Indigenous community, address, phone, email, insurance regime, chronic conditions, disability, mental health, pregnancy, cancer screening, vaccination and ICD-10 hospitalization data  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: This follows the actor's Oct 4 claim of 11M+ Nueva EPS affiliates and the Oct 5 Vaupés release, and it escalates from pressure posts to a timed ultimatum with a much larger next target. Unlike Vaupés, this capture shows a detailed field list, which points to special-category health data if genuine. The post addresses Colombians and Nueva EPS directly, so "Amazonas" here is Colombia's Amazonas department. Unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that Nueva EPS systems were breached. If authentic, affiliates in Amazonas, many in Indigenous communities, could face health-related phishing and fraud.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Colombia #NuevaEPS #Healthcare #DataLeak #Extortion #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity nitter.net/DailyDarkWeb/status/21…

⚠️ UPDATE: EXPLOITATION ATTEMPTS HIT ATLASSIAN CVE-2026-21589 (CVSS 9.3)  Previdian's honeypot network saw exploitation attempts about 2 hours after watchTowr Labs published its technical write-up on the pre-auth file-read flaw we covered on Oct 6.  What's new: • Root cause: the shared atlassian-plugins-webresource library turns "::" into "/", so "..::" sequences slip past path-traversal checks • No login needed: files inside the app server's web root can be read, incl. protected WEB-INF files • Affects Jira, Jira Service Management, Confluence, Bitbucket, Bamboo, Crowd, Crucible and Fisheye (Data Center) • In Crowd-linked setups, crowd[.]properties holds the app password in plaintext; watchTowr used it to create a user and make it a Jira admin • Previdian logged 15 attempts from 3 IPs: 38.60.157[.]86, 146.70.187[.]234, 159.26.119[.]225  Fixed versions are in our earlier post below; one correction: the Crowd 7.1 fix is 7.1.7, not 7.1.1.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: These are attempts seen on honeypots, not confirmed compromises, and the CVE is not in CISA KEV. A Nuclei scanning template is out; expect more probing. Patch now, or pull instances off the internet until you can, and check access logs per Atlassian's advisory.  Source (watchTowr Labs): labs.watchtowr.com/you-wont-… #DDW #DarkWeb #Atlassian #CVE #PatchNow nitter.net/DailyDarkWeb/status/21…

🚨 DISCORD SECURITY BOT DOUBLE COUNTER BREACHED: ~28M DISCORD ACCOUNTS TREATED AS EXPOSED  Double Counter, a server-protection bot used across Discord, says an attacker got in on Oct 4 through a vulnerable Metabase analytics tool still running on a retired, publicly reachable server, then used cloud credentials stored there.  Per its incident report (INC-2026-10-04): • About 12 GB copied from one database • ~28M Discord user IDs/usernames and ~27M IP + coarse location records treated as exposed • ~1M email addresses copied, incl. ~840K Doogle accounts • Bot token hijacked to post the attacker's links in ~50 large servers • A stolen Stripe key from a separate product was used for fraudulent charges; the two customer charges were refunded  Have I Been Pwned added the breach on Oct 7 after a dataset of 274,922 unique emails and Discord usernames was published.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: No threat actor has been named. Discord passwords were not involved, since the bot never receives them. Expect Discord-themed phishing and fake "verification" lures using the leaked usernames and emails, and don't join servers advertised in unexpected bot messages.  Official: doublecounter.gg/blog/securi… #DDW #DarkWeb #DataBreach #Discord #CyberSecurity

🇯🇵 🚨 ADVANTEST CONFIRMS PERSONAL DATA WAS STOLEN IN FEBRUARY CYBERATTACK  Advantest, the Japanese maker of semiconductor test equipment, is notifying people that data taken in a February 2026 cyberattack included their personal information, according to a notice letter dated October 6, 2026 and filed with the California Attorney General.  What Advantest says: • Advantest says it became aware in February 2026 that an unauthorized third party had accessed its systems and extracted some data from its servers; the California AG filing (Advantest America, Inc.) lists the breach date as Jan 23, 2026 • Data types listed in the notice: contact information, date of birth, Social Security numbers, national ID numbers, driver's licenses, passport numbers, medical and financial information, and other ID numbers • The incident was contained and the network restored; authorities, including law enforcement, were notified • Affected people are offered 18 months of free Kroll credit and identity monitoring (enroll by Jan 4, 2027)  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The notice does not give the number of people affected or say whether they are employees, customers or partners. Advantest says it has no information that the data was published or misused, and no group has publicly claimed the attack. Recipients should watch for phishing that uses the breach.  Official: oag.ca.gov/system/files/Adva… #DDW #DarkWeb #DataBreach #Japan #Semiconductor #CyberSecurity

🇧🇩 BANGLADESH: PATHAO ALLEGEDLY HIT WITH 133GB DATA EXTORTION, 19M USER RECORDS CLAIMED  A threat actor on an underground forum has posted a public "notice" to Pathao Limited, the Dhaka-based ride-hailing, delivery and fintech super app, claiming to hold its production data and demanding payment.  The listing claims: * ~250 million rows across 591 tables (133 GB) * A user master table of 19,063,918 accounts with emails, phone numbers, legal names, password hashes, GPS data and Facebook IDs/access tokens * 19,059,387 National ID (NID) numbers and 19,046,583 driving licence entries, plus profile photos and 5.7M home addresses * HR records for 549 employees (NID, salary, religion, emergency contacts), 17,943 merchant bank account/routing records and 845,872 direct-debit records * A 400,000 USDT ransom demand with a 24-hour deadline, and a threat to keep releasing data  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: The post lists table names and row counts, but the captured page shows no sample records, so the figures cannot be checked. A Pathao claim from what appears to be the same actor first surfaced a day earlier, and the actor says a local newspaper has already reported a service outage; Pathao has not confirmed either. If genuine, national ID, licence and address data at this scale would create serious identity-fraud and SIM-swap risk in Bangladesh. This is an unverified threat-actor claim, NOT confirmation that Pathao was breached. Users should expect Pathao-themed phishing and account-recovery scams and should change any reused passwords.  #DDW #DarkWeb #Bangladesh #Pathao #DataBreach #Extortion #ThreatIntelligence #CyberSecurity

🚨 SONICWALL PATCHES CVSS 10.0 UNAUTHENTICATED SSRF IN SMA1000 REMOTE-ACCESS GATEWAYS (CVE-2026-102255)  SonicWall released platform hotfixes on October 6, 2026 for a maximum-severity server-side request forgery flaw in its SMA1000 secure remote access appliances.  • CVE: CVE-2026-102255 (advisory SNWLID-2026-0017), CVSS 3.0 10.0 • Affected: Appliance WorkPlace interface on SMA1000 6210, 7210 and 8200v running 12.4.3-03526 or 12.5.0-02952 platform-hotfix and older • Fixed: 12.4.3-03670 and 12.5.0-03082 platform-hotfix or later • Impact: a remote, unauthenticated attacker could make the appliance send requests on their behalf, reach internal functionality and perform unauthorized operations • Same advisory: three post-auth flaws (CVE-2026-102256 RCE, CVE-2026-102257 Zip Slip, CVE-2026-102258 stored XSS) • Not affected: SMA 100 series and SSL-VPN on SonicWall firewalls  ⚠️ Analyst Note: SonicWall says there is no evidence of exploitation in the wild, and the CVE is not in CISA KEV at handoff. SMA1000 appliances have been exploited as zero-days before (CVE-2025-23006 in January 2025), so treat this as a priority patch for any internet-facing appliance.  Official: psirt.global.sonicwall.com/v… #DDW #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity #SonicWall #CVE #PatchNow

🚨 CRITICAL AUTH BYPASS IN FLEXERA FLEXNET PUBLISHER LMADMIN (CVE-2026-19572, CVSS 9.3)  Revenera (Flexera) has disclosed a critical authentication bypass in lmadmin, the license-server administration component of FlexNet Publisher, the licensing technology built into many enterprise and engineering software products.  • CVE-2026-19572: a hardcoded authentication bypass in an lmadmin SOAP handler could let an unauthenticated user obtain a privileged administrator session without valid credentials • CVSS 4.0: 9.3 (Critical); network attack, low complexity, no privileges or user interaction needed • Weakness: CWE-288 (authentication bypass using an alternate path or channel) • Affected: FlexNet Publisher lmadmin 11.19.11 and earlier (Windows, Linux, macOS and Solaris per the CVE record) • Credited to researcher Ryan Wincey (Securifera) via responsible disclosure  What to do: • Find every lmadmin instance, including license servers installed alongside third-party software • Upgrade to lmadmin 11.19.11.1, the fixed release named in Revenera's advisory • Keep the lmadmin management interface off the internet and limit it to trusted admin hosts  ⚠️ Analyst Note:  Neither the advisory nor the CVE record reports in-the-wild exploitation, and the flaw is not in CISA KEV. Because FlexNet licensing ships inside many vendors' products, lmadmin servers are easy to miss in asset inventories. An administrator session on a license server could be used to tamper with licensing configuration or disrupt the applications that depend on it.  Sources: community.revenera.com/s/art… cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-202… #DDW #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity #Flexera #FlexNet #CVE #PatchNow

🇦🇪 🚨 EVEREST RANSOMWARE GROUP CLAIMS FLYDUBAI, ALLEGES THEFT OF 4.36 GB OF FLIGHT-OPS AND CREW FILES  The Everest ransomware group has listed Dubai-based airline Flydubai (flydubai[.]com) as a victim on its leak site, claiming to hold about 4.36 GB of data across 16,517 files. Ransomware trackers first recorded the listing on Oct 6.  The group claims the files include: * Flight-operations documentation * Crew-training records and personnel exports * Manufacturer technical publications and electronic flight reference packages * Boeing engineering software  The listing says the operational material covers Boeing 737NG systems and threatens to publish the files when a countdown runs out.  The claim has not been independently verified.  ⚠️ Analyst Note: This is an unverified threat-actor claim. Flydubai has not confirmed any incident, and Everest has a history of overstating its claims. Manuals and manufacturer publications are widely shared across the aviation supply chain, so material like this could come from a partner or supplier rather than the airline's own network.  We assess this as Everest's claim only, NOT confirmation of a breach of Flydubai's systems.  If genuine, the personnel and crew-training records would put Flydubai staff at risk of targeted phishing and impersonation. Treat unexpected messages using Flydubai's name with caution.  Source: ransomware.live/id/Rmx5ZHViY… #DDW #DarkWeb #Ransomware #Everest #Flydubai #UAE #Aviation #CyberSecurity

sample_tweets.text: 🚨 BLACKNET-00 Claims Breach of South Africa's CIPC Exposing Corporate Records  The ransomware group BLACKNET-00 has claimed to have breached the systems of the Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) in South Africa, according to a post on an underground forum. The threat actor alleges that its team successfully compromised the primary databases of the authority responsible for company registration and intellectual property protection in the country.  According to the listing, the stolen data includes sensitive documents relating to thousands of registered companies. The actor claims to possess: *   Company incorporation records *   Names and identification details of directors and shareholders *   Postal and residential addresses *   Tax registration numbers *   Franchise and partnership agreements *   Intellectual property records, including registered trademarks and patents  The post further alleges that the group compromised systems of affiliated organizations, naming specific entities such as IPUTHA TRADING, EADMIN CENTRE, JACOBS AANVULLINGS PTY LTD, and DATAEQ PTY LTD. The threat actor outlines several potential fraudulent activities enabled by this data, including opening bank accounts or shell companies in the names of registered directors, applying for loans using company financial records, and impersonating directors to sign forged contracts. The group also claims the ability to forge official documents bearing the Commission’s seals and signatures.  CIPC is a critical government agency in South Africa, serving as the central repository for all business registrations and intellectual property rights in the country. A breach of this magnitude would expose vast amounts of Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and corporate secrets, posing significant risks for identity fraud, corporate espionage, and financial crimes. BLACKNET-00 is a known ransomware affiliate that has been active in targeting government and enterprise sectors globally, often publishing breach notices on darkweb forums to pressure victims into paying ransoms. At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by the CIPC or other security researchers.

🚨 A dark web post is not proof of a breach. Recent underground listings have put major organizations and datasets in the spotlight.  Samples, dataset age, technical indicators, credential validity, and internal telemetry can make the difference between a credible exposure, recycled data, and an unsupported forum post.  We examined the recent claims and what security teams should actually look for when assessing them.  🔗 Read the analysis: threatmon.io/nhs-samsung-cia… #DarkWeb #ThreatIntelligence #CyberThreatIntelligence #DataBreach #ThreatMon

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Massive Pathao Breach, Demands 400k USDT Ransom  A threat actor has posted a detailed extortion notice on an underground forum, claiming to have compromised the production infrastructure of Pathao Limited, a major ride-hailing and logistics company based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. The actor alleges that they have gained full control of the company's production estate and are currently executing "kill loops" to disrupt services, a claim that aligns with recent outage reports attributed to the group "New Age."  According to the post, the attacker has exfiltrated approximately 250 million rows of data totaling 133 GB across 591 tables. The alleged data dump includes highly sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) for nearly 19 million users, including:  *   Full names, email addresses, phone numbers, and home addresses *   National ID (NID) numbers and driving license details *   Facebook IDs and access tokens *   Bcrypt password hashes *   Profile photos and GPS location data  The notice further claims the theft of internal administrative and financial records, including:  *   5,825 admin backend accounts with login credentials and reset codes *   HRIS records for 549 employees, containing salary, religion, and emergency contacts *   Bank account and routing information for 17,943 merchants *   Direct-debit records and wallet transaction logs *   Delivery tracking events and driver login query logs  Pathao is one of Bangladesh's largest digital service providers, operating in ride-hailing, food delivery, and e-commerce sectors. The exposure of National ID numbers and banking details for millions of users could facilitate significant identity theft and financial fraud if the data is authentic.  The attacker demands a settlement of 400,000 USDT via TRC-20 within 24 hours to halt daily public dumps and restore access to locked application nodes. The post warns that failure to pay will result in the release of NID, bank, and HR data packs, followed by the remainder of the dataset. At the time of reporting, Pathao Limited has not publicly confirmed the breach, and the extent of the compromise remains unverified.

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Breach of South Korean E-Commerce Platform Metree  A post on an underground forum alleges that the customer database of metree.co.kr, a leading online shopping platform in South Korea, has been compromised. The threat actor claims to have obtained over 1 million unique records containing sensitive personally identifiable information (PII) of the platform's users.  According to the listing, the leaked data includes: - User IDs - Email addresses - Full names - Phone numbers - Zip codes - Physical addresses  The actor further alleges that a separate subset of 30,000 records contains additional sensitive data, specifically bank account numbers and dates of birth. The post describes metree.co.kr as an e-commerce and technology company that operates direct retail sales, a marketplace for third-party sellers, and its own logistics network.  Metree is a significant player in the South Korean e-commerce sector, known for its integrated logistics and marketplace model. If authentic, the exposure of banking details and full PII for hundreds of thousands of users could facilitate targeted phishing, identity theft, and financial fraud. The threat actor has provided an onionmail address for contact, suggesting an intent to sell or leak the data further.  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by metree.co.kr or security researchers.  #DataBreach #Metree #SouthKorea #ECommerce #PII #DarkWeb #ThreatIntelligence

🚨 Alleged Bangladesh Union Tax Database Leak Exposes 563,000 Records  A post on an underground forum claims the theft of a large-scale database from Bangladesh’s uniontax.gov.bd portal. The threat actor alleges that the compromised dataset contains 563,000 total records, including 207,000 unique phone numbers and 252,000 unique national ID card numbers.  According to the listing, the database comprises over 115 columns of sensitive personal and administrative data. The exposed fields reportedly include: *   Applicant names and father's names *   National ID numbers and birth certificate numbers *   Dates of birth, religion, and gender *   Full residential addresses and mobile numbers *   Administrative details such as union, division, district, and upazila names *   Chairman names and payment/tax records  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by the Bangladesh government or cybersecurity authorities. The identity of the threat actor remains unknown, with no prior documented history provided in the source material.  #DataBreach #Bangladesh #UnionTax #PII #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity

🚨 Alleged 10 Million Record Breach of South African Firm Thrive Online Group Listed for Sale  A darkweb forum post claims that a massive dataset containing personal information of over 10 million South African citizens has been stolen from Thrive Online Group (thriveonlinegroup.com) and is currently being offered for sale. The threat actor alleges the dataset comprises 17 million total lines, with 10 million unique records of personal data, including full names, phone numbers, and South African ID card numbers.  According to the listing, the exposed data includes the following fields: - Full name (First and Surname) - Phone number (10 million+ unique entries) - Email address (331,000 unique entries) - ID card number (6.9 million unique entries)  At the time of reporting, Thrive Online Group has not publicly confirmed the breach, and the authenticity of the dataset remains unverified. The incident highlights the ongoing risk to consumer data held by third-party marketing agencies in the region.  #DataBreach #SouthAfrica #ThriveOnlineGroup #IdentityTheft #DarkWeb #CyberSecurity

🚨 Threat Actor Claims Leak of Russian Ministry of Industry and Trade Military Data  A darkweb forum post alleges the theft and sale of sensitive data from the Russian Ministry of Industry and Trade. According to the listing, the actor claims to possess a 1.62 GB dataset comprising 1,502 files, which they describe as "original-source material" acquired through independent work rather than resold from other actors.  The post details that the alleged data dump includes highly sensitive defense-related information, such as: - Arms and military-equipment licenses - Suppliers for defence orders - Mobilisation reservation of officers - Defense-industry registers - Service licenses for arms and military equipment - Defence-order reports covering the period 2020–2026  At the time of reporting, the alleged breach has not been independently verified by Russian authorities or cybersecurity researchers. The threat actor’s identity remains unknown, and no prior track record or reputation was established in the provided intelligence.  #DataLeak #Russia #DefenseSector #DarkWeb #MinPromTorg #CyberSecurity

⚠️ Threat Actor Claims CIA and FBI Data for Sale on Underground Forum  A post published on an underground forum claims that data belonging to the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) and the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is available for purchase. The listing, posted on October 4, 2026, by a user identified as “carrion_secalin,” explicitly titled the offer “CIA.GOV AND FBI.GOV For Sale” and stated, “I have ‘apply.fbijobs.gov’ from my ShinyHunters group because our leader chickened out; while I hacked the admin account for ‘cia.gov’ using a web cache WAF bypass method.”  The source material is limited to the subject line and metadata; no additional details were provided regarding data types, the volume of records, or the method of acquisition. This claim implies that the U.S.’s critical national security infrastructure may be at risk and, if verified, would constitute a serious security breach.

### 2. 주요 위협 행위자 / 캠페인

- **Unknown (Chinese-speaking)**: [Crowdstrike Blog](https://www.crowdstrike.com/en-us/blog/unknown-threat-actor-uses-artex-to-target-south-korean-finance/) - AI 기반 침투 도구 ARTEX를 활용해 한국 금융권을 타겟팅함.
- **Blinder Tunnel**: [Unit42](https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/blinder-tunnel-targets-critical-infrastructure/) - 이란 연계 그룹으로, 가짜 채용 공고를 미끼로 이라크 인프라를 공격함.

### 3. 한국 관련 위협
- **한국 금융권 타겟팅**: 공격자가 AI 침투 도구 ARTEX를 사용하여 한국 금융기관을 해킹했으며, 서버에서 AI 작업 기록 및 유출 정보 판매처 탐색 정황이 발견됨([데일리시큐](https://www.dailysecu.com/news/articleView.html?idxno=208781)).
